reason.observation: All eight failures are raw central-difference gradient checks dominated by gc. Halving the original step gives approximately factor4 error reduction; independent scalar-qT and projected-P AD gradients agree to about6.1e-16 on these fixed rows.
reason.inference: This is consistent with second-order central-stencil truncation, not evidence that the original failed derivative checks passed. No extrapolated candidate is used to set this policy.

preservation: The physical qT mapping, all initial samples/rows, cut values, angles, prediction/derivative formulas and base contract bytes remain unchanged. Preserve original FAIL and all raw central-stencil operands. This addendum prospectively replaces only the raw second-order reference acceptance method.

policy.grid_origin: Retain both original steps and add their fixed halving; no error-dependent step selection
policy.central_gradient: D_h[j]=(f(theta+h*e_j)-f(theta-h*e_j))/(2h) for every one of thirteen coordinates
policy.fourth_order: R_h=(4*D_(h/2)-D_h)/3, entrywise; retain R_h and R_(h/2) from the three central steps
policy.Taylor_basis: For a smooth interior scalar entry, D_h=fprime+h^2*fthird/6+h^4*ffifth/120+O(h^6). Thus R_h=fprime-h^4*ffifth/480+O(h^6). The same entrywise argument applies to directional Jacobian differences.
policy.acceptance: Both coarse and refined fourth-order gradients/HVPs must meet the original fixed target against the candidate AD result, and both adjacent fourth-order differences must meet that same target. Every case and all thirteen coordinates are required; never choose a favorable stencil or discard a failed case.
policy.raw_central_stencil_scope: Retain values and errors with target-met booleans as diagnostics. A raw stencil that misses1e-7 remains recorded as missing1e-7; the previous raw-only report remains FAIL. Only the explicitly labelled fourth-order method is eligible for the new reference gate.
policy.unsupported: No boundary derivative recovery, differentiated cuts/kinematics, global identifiability, production G2AD or interval-coverage claim

closed_functions: x^3 at x=0.01: second-order bias is h^2 and fourth-order formula recovers3*x^2
exp(7*x) at x=0.01: independently known derivative7*exp(7*x)
validation.fixed_rows: Use exactly the four cases,13-vector,direction and momentum quadrature policy from the unchanged parent contract
validation.preservation_checks: Compare all retained absolute-yield/refinement vectors, AD gradients/HVPs, initial two raw finite-difference records and predictions bitwise against the original report; new source/status bindings necessarily differ.

limitations: A higher-order numerical reference is not a change to physical accuracy or experimental admission
Prepared evolution rows and initial functions are shared evidence; evolution is not independently solved
